_comment: Notes emitted as comments above a labelled address by tools/disasm_all.py. Key: 'BB:AAAA' (hex bank, CPU address). Each note states what the instructions do and its evidence level. 'static reading' = read from the instructions only, not confirmed by running the game. Notes ending '(C1, E-0357)' were written by hand after reading the whole routine: the mechanics are a static reading, and what the routine is for (the scene, menu or state it serves, taken from its messages, flags and callers) is a C1 hypothesis.
00:0000: C2 static reading (E-0007): rst $00 pops its return address as the base of an inline word table, indexes it by A (entry = base + 2*A), preserves DE, and jumps to the entry.
00:0010: C2 static reading (E-0007): rst $10 selects ROM bank B, calls the code at HL, then restores the caller's bank (saved from $4000, which holds each bank's own number, E-0006).
00:0B18: C2 static reading (E-0014): selects ROM bank B and copies C bytes from [DE] to [HL] (C = 0 copies 256), then restores the caller's bank.
00:0B2B: C2 static reading (E-0014): like Func_000_0B18, but before each byte waits for STAT ($FF41) bit 1 to clear with interrupts disabled, so HL can be VRAM.
00:0B46: C2 static reading (E-0014): selects ROM bank B; C times reads a byte from [DE] (advancing DE once), waits for STAT bit 1 to clear, ORs the byte into [HL] and advances HL; then restores the caller's bank. Clobbers B.
00:0C5A: C2 static reading (E-0016): takes the lock byte $FFD6 (spins while it is non-zero), calls Func_000_0C69, then clears the lock.
00:0C69: C2 (E-0016: static reading; 141 emulated calls matched tools/lzss_gfx.py byte for byte): expands the compressed stream at [DE] in ROM bank B into memory at [HL] with a plain store per byte (RAM destination). Header and format: see Func_000_0DA8. Restores the caller's bank on return.
00:0CF5: C2 (E-0016): the same expansion as Func_000_0C69 but for VRAM destinations: each store waits for STAT ($FF41) bit 1 to clear with interrupts disabled, back-references read the already-written VRAM, and the lock byte $FFD6 is taken on entry and cleared on exit.
00:0DA8: C2 static reading (E-0016): selects ROM bank B, then reads the compressed-stream header from [DE]: u16 output size into BC, a marker byte into $FFBB. Saves the destination start (HL) in $FFBC/$FFBD and $FFC3/$FFC4 and the destination end (HL + size) in $FFC1/$FFC2.
00:0B6C: C2 static reading (E-0014): switches to the ROM bank held in $D7FE, reads the word at [HL] into B (low address) and C (next address), leaves HL unchanged, restores the caller's bank. $D7FE is therefore the data-bank variable for reads through HL; 30 call sites.
00:3354: C2 static reading, and 495 emulated sound starts agree (E-0018): starts sound id A (kept in $DD10). Finds A's range in SoundBankTable, switches to that bank, takes the 4-byte record at (array + 4*(A - first id)), and copies it into the channel-state slot at $DC00 + record byte 0 (record byte 1 to slot +2, the track pointer to +3/+4, this bank to +5). Returns A + 1.
00:33E8: C1 (E-0018): appears to be the sound engine's update routine. It switches to the bank in $FFDD, walks the channel-state slots at $DC00 and writes the sound registers (including $FF1A). Identified from those writes and from the banks it reads at runtime ($40-$43 via the tables above); not decoded further.
00:35CD: C2 static reading and 5,154 emulated fetches agree (E-0019): fetches the next track event of the current channel. The position in $FFD8/$FFD9 counts 2-byte events from the track start ($FFDB/$FFDC), the event address is base + 2*position, and the first byte selects the command (see tools/sound_tracks.py).
00:3554: C2 static reading (E-0019): channel start. Reads the 4-byte track header (byte 0 low nibble -> $FFDF, byte 1 -> duty bits of $FFDE (wave: $FFE6), byte 2 swapped -> $FFE0, byte 3 -> $FFE2) and begins playback at event 2 ($FFD8 = 2).
00:3938: C2 (E-0019: formula matched 1,928 of 1,928 emulated notes): pitch for a note event. The semitone (low nibble of the first byte, 0-11) indexes the period table at $3B5C ($3B74 when $FFDE bit 4 is set), the value is shifted right by the octave (high nibble) and subtracted from $0800 to give the frequency register value in HL. Noise-channel notes use $38A0.
00:3DAE: C2 static reading (E-0019): address of a label slot: HL = $DCC0 + channel*12 + (B & $0F)*3. A slot holds a repeat counter and a saved position (2 bytes); used by the FD, B0 and B1-BF commands.
1B:5352: C1 static reading (E-0197): not reached from any traced code, pointer or far call found; the bytes after the word list at $51B6 decode as one routine: clear $6F bytes from wScreenState, decompress bank $46 $4001 to $8800, far-call F1:$4AA8, LoadPalette0FromData_3, then wait on wTextWindowState and jp $077A

00:015A: Power-on start-up, then the main loop. Start-up: masks interrupts, clears WRAM, HRAM and SRAM banks 0 and 2, installs the OAM DMA routine, clears the tile area (and on CGB the BG map attributes in VRAM bank 1), selects game mode 5 (the title screen) and maps ROM and SRAM bank defaults. On CGB it loads palette 0; otherwise DetectSGB, and on a Super Game Boy it sends the start-up packet sets, transfers the border tiles and map, and sets the palettes. Every mode then starts here: clear the screen, sprites, scroll and fade, run the mode's start-up routine (RunGameModeInit), reset the frame counters. The loop halts until each interrupt (advancing the random table with NextTableByte when not linked); the per-frame work runs in VBlankHandler. When wModeChangeRequest is set and no fade is in progress (wFadeState 0 or bit 7 set), it masks interrupts, sends SGB packet set 0 and restarts at the screen clear for the new mode. (C1, E-0357)

00:0646: Reads the joypad of each Super Game Boy player, up to four (B = 4). Each pass reads the player number from rP1, selects the button lines ($20) and the direction lines ($10) and combines them into one byte; that player's 2-byte slot of wSGBJoypad1 gets the held buttons in its first byte and the newly pressed ones (held now, not before) in its second. It stops early when rP1 reads back the value it started with, which is when the SGB has cycled through the connected players. (C1, E-0357)
00:077A: Turns the screen back on after a mode change and re-enables interrupts with the mask in A: when linked it first re-synchronises with the partner (the serial handshake at ClearSGBPacketBuffer_WaitSerialTransferDone), then sets LCDC bit 7 and sends the SGB unfreeze packet, clears rIF, writes rIE and enables interrupts. Not part of ClearSGBPacketBuffer; it only follows it in the ROM. (C1, E-0357)
00:07AA: Switches the LCD on (sets bit 7 of wLCDCShadow and copies it to rLCDC); on a Super Game Boy it also sends packet set 1 and waits. The 11 bytes after its ret are never reached; as code they would be ret / xor a / ldh [rIF], a / ldh a, [rIE] / and $F7 / ldh [rIE], a / ret (clear the serial interrupt enable). (C1, E-0357)
00:07D8: Clears pending interrupts (rIF = 0) and enables those in A (rIE = A). (C1, E-0357)
00:085C: VBlank step that uploads sprite palettes on CGB. If bit 7 of wOBJPaletteUploadRequest is set, it uploads one palette (8 bytes; bits 3-5 of the request choose it, and the request also goes to rOBPI) from wOBJPaletteBuffer; otherwise all eight (64 bytes) from wOBJPaletteBuffer. Each byte waits for rSTAT mode below 2 with interrupts off before it goes to rOBPD. (C1, E-0357)
00:0FC1: Super Game Boy step of the palette fade: fades the colour groups chosen by bits 0-3 of wFadeMask (8 bytes each, see StepFade_WriteFadeStepSize; groups 2 and 3 only when bit 4 is set), then sends the colours at wOBJPaletteBuffer as SGB packet $01 (PAL01); when bit 4 is set it also sends wOBJPaletteBuffer + $10 as packet $09 (PAL23). (C1, E-0357)
00:1040: Fades one SGB palette group of four colours: StepFade_AdjustColorChannelForFade for the colour at the current offset, then the offset (wFadeStepSize) moves on by 2 bytes per colour; the code falls through the two increments to the next colours. (C1, E-0357)
00:1049: Moves the fade offset wFadeStepSize to the next colour (2 bytes) and falls through to fade it. (C1, E-0357)
00:1051: Fades one 15-bit colour for the SGB path: takes the target colour from wOBJPaletteBuffer + $20 + wFadeStepSize, moves each of its red, green and blue channels by wFadeLevel with AdjustColorChannelForFade, packs them back and stores the result at the same offset of wOBJPaletteBuffer. (C1, E-0357)
00:10C7: CGB path of the fade: far-calls StepCGBFade, which moves every palette one level toward the fade target. (C1, E-0357)
00:10CE: DMG fade step toward white (wFadeMode bit 7 clear; set means toward black, LightenDMGShade_CheckFadeState). Waits wFadeDelay frames per step; each step redraws the chosen DMG palettes and moves wFadeLevel up (fading out) or down (fading in, wFadeState bit 7); the fade ends (wFadeState = 0) when the level reaches 4 or wraps below 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:116D: DMG fade step toward black (wFadeMode bit 7 set): the same timing as the fade toward white, but each step redraws the palettes with DarkenDMGPaletteByFadeLevel; the fade ends at level 4 or below 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:11B4: Redraws the DMG palettes the fade affects: for each of bits 0-2 of wFadeMode it darkens the matching saved palette in wFadeDMGPalettes (BGP, OBP0, OBP1) by wFadeLevel into wDMGPaletteBGP and the bytes after it. (C1, E-0357)
00:137D: Music volume fade, run once per frame from StepFade. When wSoundFadeLevel is set (and not bit 7, and no field set-up is in progress) it waits wSoundFadeTarget frames per step, then lowers each stereo side of the master volume (rNR50) by one, keeping the left/right enable bits; when the volume reaches 0, or wSoundFadeTimer steps have passed, the fade stops (wSoundFadeLevel = 0). (C1, E-0357)
00:14D1: Serial link re-synchronisation after a mode change (only when wLinkMode is set; otherwise it just clears the link state). With only the serial interrupt enabled it marks the link busy, lets the clock-receiving side wait about 24,576 loop passes, then exchanges a greeting: $F5 in link session 5, otherwise $70 | wIsCGB, expecting $70 or $71 back. It settles which side drives the clock (wLinkRole bit 1) from the two consoles' CGB flags, clears the busy bits, and resets wLinkExchangeState and the 14 joypad bytes from wJoypadHeld. (C1, E-0357)
00:1583: Link greeting exchange: sends $70 | wIsCGB (driving the clock when wLinkRole bit 1 is clear, otherwise waiting for the partner's clock) and counts in wLinkTimer until the transfer completes (wLinkStatus bit 6). If the 16-bit count reaches $FF00 it gives up and sets wLinkFrameCounterHi to 2; otherwise returns A = 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:15C2: Sends the link acknowledgement byte $F5 (as clock receiver or driver, by wLinkRole bit 1) and waits until the transfer completes (wLinkStatus bit 6). (C1, E-0357)
00:1A73: Draws a map's special 2x2 marker, unless wMapType bit 7 is set. The table after the routine (code at $1AB4) holds 3-byte entries (map id, position, screen) for 11 maps ending with $FF; for the entry matching hMapId it draws the marker with LoadMapScreen_WriteSVBK, passing the entry's index in hTemp0. In a key world (wKeyWorldActive) whose key is that index + 1, the position comes from wKeyWorldGoal instead. What the marker shows in play is not yet confirmed. (C1, E-0357)
00:1AD6: Draws the marker of LoadMapScreen_WriteTemp0 when its screen byte (screen X in the high nibble, Y in the low) matches the current screen. The position byte's low nibble gives the metatile row and its high nibble the column; tiles $46 $47 over $56 $57 go into wScreenTileBuffer, and on CGB the same cells of the attribute copy (WRAM bank 2, $D000 upwards) get palette 3 (entries 4 and 10), 5 (entries 5-7) or 1 (others). (C1, E-0357)
00:1B6F: After the story flag EVENT_SCENE_STRONGEST_MASTER is set, patches two map screens at screen X 0: map $0D gets tiles $44 $45 over $46 $47 at wScreenTileBuffer + $14A, and map $05 gets $78 $79 over $7A $7B at wScreenTileBuffer + $32. What the changed tiles show is not yet confirmed. (C1, E-0357)
00:1D90: Debug map editor check of the edit position. With bank $11 mapped it follows entry hTemp0 of the pointer table at $44B8 to a map record, and returns A = 1 when the position is outside it: wDebugValue1 not below the record's byte 6 (its width) or wDebugValue3 not below byte 7 (its height), or the 3-byte cell at row wDebugValue3, column wDebugValue1 holds a zero word. The cell table is chosen through the record's pointer at offset 16 and the first set bit of the byte it points to. Otherwise returns A = 0. Restores the ROM bank. (C1, E-0357)
00:228A: Loads the sprite tiles and palettes of the party members who follow the player in the field. For each member of wPartyList it writes the species word to a list from wPartyList + 3 and decompresses the species' sprite (MonsterSpriteTable, bank $04) to VRAM, $100 bytes apart from vTiles0 + $100; on CGB it copies the species' 8-byte palette from bank $27 ($7328 + species * 8) to the member's object palette (member index + 1). A member whose SRAM status byte has bit 7 set gets $FFFF in the list and a fixed graphic and palette from bank $7E instead; what that bit means is not yet confirmed. (C1, E-0357)
00:2447: The end of CopyItemNameToDE: follows the string pointer, copies the item name up to and including its $F0 terminator to DE, and restores the caller's ROM bank. (C1, E-0357)
00:2582: The common exit of StatInterruptHandler: restores the WRAM bank and the saved registers and returns from the interrupt. It is also split 0 (no split). (C1, E-0357)
00:2589: STAT split 1: does nothing (jumps to the common exit). (C1, E-0357)
00:258B: STAT split 2, a horizontal wave: on each interrupt sets rSCX to the byte at wBGPaletteCopy + rLY (the buffer here holds per-line scroll values) and moves the LYC line on by 2; after line $8F it restores rSCX from hScrollX and restarts at line 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:25AA: STAT split 3, a vertical wave: on each interrupt sets rSCY to the byte at wBGPaletteCopy + rLY and moves the LYC line on by 2; after line $80 it restores rSCY from hScrollY and restarts at line 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:28BD: Draws one glyph of text over the tile being built: finds glyph L's 16-byte font tile (GlyphTileSourceForL), backs the destination up one tile and ORs the 16 bytes into VRAM, waiting for VRAM access before each byte; in byte 4 (B = $0D) it also clears bit 1. Stores the end address in wTextGlyphDestLo/Hi for the next glyph. (C1, E-0357)
00:2D4A: Draws the yes/no choice window: uploads the two choice tiles from wScriptTileBuf0/1 and two more from bank $1F, then writes the window from TextPromptWindowTiles to the BG map 14 columns right of the scroll position ($FD starts a new row, $FE ends); on CGB it writes the attributes from TextPromptWindowAttrs to VRAM bank 1 in the same way. (C1, E-0357)
00:2FA7: The thousands digit of WriteBCAsDecimalString: BC / 1000 is stored as a digit and BC keeps the remainder. (C1, E-0357)
00:2FB0: The hundreds digit of WriteBCAsDecimalString: BC / 100. (C1, E-0357)
00:2FB9: The tens digit of WriteBCAsDecimalString: BC / 10. (C1, E-0357)
00:2FC2: The ones digit of WriteBCAsDecimalString: stores what is left in C. (C1, E-0357)
00:32DB: Sets which sound channels to wait for (wSoundChannelMask = B, and C into wSoundChannelMaskCount) and clears the set of channels that have finished. InitSoundHardware calls it with BC = 0. (C1, E-0357)
00:32E8: Marks the current sound channel (wSoundChannelIndex) as finished: ORs bit (index) into wSoundChannelsDone. (C1, E-0357)
00:32FE: When every channel in wSoundChannelMask has finished, writes the low nibble of wSoundChannelMaskCount into the low nibble of byte 6 of each of those channels' 32-byte slots in wSoundChannelSlots, then clears the mask; it always clears wSoundChannelsDone. What byte 6 controls is not yet known. (C1, E-0357)
00:334B: The second half of StartMusic: StartSound for the id after the first, so a two-part sound (ids A and A + 1) starts together. (C1, E-0357)
00:335D: The body of StartSound. It walks SoundBankTable (4-byte entries) to the range that holds wSoundId, maps that range's bank, and reads the sound's 4-byte record: the channel slot, a flags byte and the track pointer. If the slot is already in use, the flags' low two bits pick which stereo bits of wSoundEngineMode to clear ($EE, $DD, $BB or $77). It then fills the 32-byte slot in wSoundChannelSlots: cleared position, flags, track pointer, the track's bank, $FF in byte 11 and cleared timers. Restores the ROM bank and returns wSoundId + 1. (C1, E-0357)
00:33FD: One pass of SoundTick for the current channel slot (HL). An unused slot (both first bytes $FF) is skipped. Otherwise the slot's 32 bytes are copied into the HRAM work area from $FFD8 (hTrackPosLo and the bytes after it), the track's bank is mapped, and the channel's hardware number (flags & 3) gives its register base (5 bytes per channel) and its bit in the stereo mask. A slot whose track position is 0 starts from its track header (StartChannelFromTrackHeader). Otherwise it runs the vibrato counter, adds the tempo nibble to a tick accumulator (a tick happens when it passes $10), counts down the note and wait timers, steps the envelope, and fetches the next event when the note ends. (C1, E-0357)
00:349C: A channel's track has nothing more to wait for: marks the channel as finished (SoundTick_WriteSoundChannelsDone) and goes on to the next slot. (C1, E-0357)
00:349F: Starts the next note: reloads the note timer from hSndNoteLength and fetches the next track event (SoundNextEvent). (C1, E-0357)
00:34A8: Envelope step: when the envelope counter reaches the value in the low nibble of hSndEnvFlags - 1, it recomputes the envelope (SoundTick_WriteSndEnvelopeReloadAndSndEnvelope) and writes it to the channel if it changed. (C1, E-0357)
00:34BA: Counts down hSndWaitTicks; when it reaches 0 and the channel has no envelope steps (hSndEnvFlags high nibble 0) the channel is marked finished. (C1, E-0357)
00:34C7: End of a channel's pass. For the wave channel (hardware channel 2, slot 2 or later, not muted) whose wave set changed (wSoundWaveReload and hSndSweepOrWave different from the last one), it switches the wave channel off, loads the new 16-byte wave pattern and switches it back on. It adds the channel to the mask of channels this frame has handled (wSoundSkipMaskA), then copies the 32 HRAM work bytes back into the channel's slot. (C1, E-0357)
00:352F: Moves to the next of the 6 channel slots (32 bytes on); after the last it applies the stereo mask: wSoundEngineMode keeps only the channels that played (wSoundSkipMaskA) and goes to rNR51. Restores the ROM bank and checks whether a waited-for group of channels has finished (SoundTick_WriteSoundChannelsDoneAndSoundChannelMask). (C1, E-0357)
00:3989: The high byte of a note's frequency: H & 7 with bit 7 set (restart the channel). (C1, E-0357)
00:398E: Writes the frequency high byte (register offset 4, $14) for the current channel, keeping it in hSndFreqHi, and clears the length bits of the duty register so the note plays without a length cut-off. (C1, E-0357)
00:3998: Sets the current channel's stereo bits in wSoundEngineMode from hSndPanning: the channel's bits (wSoundNoteWork) are replaced by the matching bits of hSndPanning. (C1, E-0357)
00:39AB: Restarts the wave channel's note: clears rNR31 (the sound length); if the wave channel is not running (rNR52 bit 2 clear) it writes the high frequency byte with the restart bit, otherwise without it. (C1, E-0357)
00:39B9: The volume slide of a note (not on the wave channel): every hSndPitchSlideTime ticks the envelope's start volume (high nibble of hSndEnvelope) moves one step up while hSndPitchSlide is positive and one step down while it is negative (bit 7), stopping at 15 or 0, and the new envelope is written to the channel. The names of these HRAM bytes say pitch; the code changes the volume. (C1, E-0357)
00:39F8: The pitch offset of a note in progress (not on the noise channel), applied when the note timer has run out and the channel flags' high nibble is not 0: adds the entry of SoundPitchOffsetRows chosen by that nibble and the low nibble of wSoundTickBuf to the frequency low byte and writes it (register offset 3). Skipped when the channel is muted this frame. (C1, E-0357)
00:3A21: After a note's pitch is set: the wave channel goes to its volume write (WriteChannelRegisterC_ReadSndEnvelope); a channel with vibrato depth goes to SoundTick_CheckSndVibratoDelay; otherwise the envelope is written. (C1, E-0357)
00:3A57: Writes hSndEnvelope to the channel's envelope register (offset 2, $12); for the wave channel this is its output level. (C1, E-0357)
00:3A69: Wave-channel volume from the modulation step E: the level (E / 2 + 2) in the high nibble is written only when it is at least hSndEnvelope; its level bits ($60) go to rNR32. (C1, E-0357)
00:3A7A: Per-tick checks of a playing note: skipped when the channel is muted; a note with frequency 0 (a rest) silences the channel's envelope; the wave channel goes on to SoundTick_CheckSndVibratoDelay; other channels only when they have vibrato depth. (C1, E-0357)
00:3A94: The volume modulation step of a note. From hSndVibratoCounter and the delay hSndVibratoDelay it builds a 4-bit position, looks up the modulation row chosen by hSndWaveParam in SoundModulationTable, combines the entry with the envelope's start volume through SoundEnvelopeScaleTable and writes the result to the channel's envelope register (or, for the wave channel, its output level). Called vibrato by the HRAM names; what it changes is the volume. (C1, E-0357)
00:3B39: A rest: unless the channel is muted this frame, writes envelope 0 (silence) to the channel. (C1, E-0357)
00:3B41: Unless the channel is muted this frame, clears the channel's stereo bits (wSoundSkipMaskB) in wSoundEngineMode, silencing it on both sides. (C1, E-0357)
00:3D7C: Loads a new wave pattern when hSndSweepOrWave differs from the last one used (wSoundEventArg): records it and switches the wave channel off before the pattern is written. (C1, E-0357)
00:3D8D: Copies a 16-byte wave pattern to wave RAM (rWAVE): the set chosen by the high nibble of hSndWaveParam in SoundWaveSetTable, then the pattern at offset DE within it. (C1, E-0357)
00:3DC8: Recomputes the envelope for an envelope step: (reload nibble + 1) * (start volume + 1) / 16, at least 1, becomes the new start volume (high nibble of hSndEnvelope); hSndEnvelopeReload keeps its low nibble and takes the old start volume as its high nibble. Keeps BC and DE. (C1, E-0357)
12:4001: Runs SCRIPT_COUNTDOWN_MESSAGE: open message $10 in the current message group, then run its box until idle and end the command. wScriptStep selects the two stages. (C1, E-0358)
12:4009: Opens message $10 in the group already in wMessageGroup and advances to the shared message-wait stage. It does not select a new group. (C1, E-0358)
12:4013: Runs SCRIPT_ENCOUNTER_MESSAGE: open message $0F in the current message group, then share CountdownMessage's wait-and-finish stage. (C1, E-0358)
12:401B: Shared closing stage for CountdownMessage and EncounterCounterMessage. Runs the message box with freeze flag A = 0; returns while it is active, and ends the script command with wScriptStartRequest = $80 only when the runner returns carry (idle). (C1, E-0358)
12:4026: Opens message $0F without changing wMessageGroup, then advances to the shared message-wait stage. (C1, E-0358)
12:4030: Starts a random-battle transition on script step 0. wMapType bit 7 selects intro 1 instead of 0; after NextRandomSeed, bit 0 of wKeyRandomLo selects transition substep 0 or 2. Saves the field screen and enters mode 3, then advances the step. On a later call, ends this command with wScriptStartRequest = $80. (C1, E-0358)
12:4064: Runs SCRIPT_OBJECT_PATH_1C, a twelve-stage player-and-follower path. Hop the player and each follower in turn, leave for map $00 screen (0,2) at ($70,$F0), arrange the entry line, then hop them again and finish. wScriptStep selects the stage; hop stages assume wScriptParam0 starts at 0. (C1, E-0358)
12:4080: Last entry hop: face follower 3 down, add one to its Y, then apply the hop curve to that same Y. The curve helper advances to FinishObjectPath after sixteen calls from phase 0. (C1, E-0358)
12:4092: Entry hop for follower 2: face it down, apply the curve to its Y and add one to that Y; follower 3 also adds one to Y. Once the curve resets its phase, a two-monster party skips follower 3's hop and goes straight to FinishObjectPath. (C1, E-0358)
12:40B8: Entry hop for follower 1: face it down, apply the curve to its Y and add one to that Y; followers 2 and 3 also add one to Y. On curve completion, a one-monster party skips the other followers' hops and finishes. (C1, E-0358)
12:40E1: Entry hop for the player: face down, apply the curve to hPlayerY, then increment the player's and all three followers' Y bytes. Only the curve helper advances the stage, after sixteen calls from phase 0. (C1, E-0358)
12:40FC: Moves the player and all three followers one pixel down per call. Advances when the updated hPlayerY equals $20; this is an equality check on an eight-bit coordinate, not a clamp. (C1, E-0358)
12:4115: After the fade, face the player and all followers up and place the followers at Y = $E0, $D0, $C0. Set the player's moving bit and advance to walking the entry line; the player's coordinates come from the warp. (C1, E-0358)
12:413C: Moves the player and all followers down one pixel, facing follower 3 up. When follower 3's updated Y equals $B0, request map $00 screen (0,2), destination ($70,$F0), transition kind 0, and start the fade that advances the script. Other Y values return without starting a warp. (C1, E-0358)
12:4177: Outgoing follower-3 hop: face it right and increment its X while the curve changes its Y. The player and followers 1 and 2 increment Y; followers 1 and 2 face up. AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase supplies the shared sixteen-call stage timing. (C1, E-0358)
12:41AA: Outgoing follower-2 hop: update the follower chain from the player's pre-move Y, face follower 1 up, increment the player's Y, and apply the curve to follower 2's Y. Finish through AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase. (C1, E-0358)
12:41CC: Outgoing follower-1 hop: update the follower chain using the player's pre-move Y, face the player up, increment hPlayerY, and apply the curve to follower 1's Y. Finish through AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase; facing and coordinate change are preserved as written. (C1, E-0358)
12:41ED: Begin the outgoing path by setting the player's moving bit. Update followers using the player's pre-move X, apply the hop curve to hPlayerY, increment hPlayerX, and use AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase to advance after sixteen calls from phase 0. (C1, E-0358)
12:4210: Runs SCRIPT_OBJECT_PATH_1B, a twelve-stage player-and-follower path. Hop the outgoing chain, leave for map $1A screen (2,0) at ($60,$B0), arrange the entry line, walk to Y = $50, then hop left and finish. Several stages decrement follower Y rather than X; these stores are preserved, not inferred from their facing. (C1, E-0358)
12:422C: Shared final stage of ObjectPath1B and ObjectPath1C: clear the player's moving bit and end the script command with wScriptStartRequest = $80. Leaves the hop phase and follower records as the preceding stage produced them. (C1, E-0358)
12:4238: Last entry hop: face follower 3 left and decrement its X, while applying the curve to its Y. The curve helper advances to FinishObjectPath on completion. Follower 3's direct movement changes from the Y decrements in the preceding stages to an X decrement here. (C1, E-0358)
12:424B: Entry hop for follower 2: face it left, curve its Y and decrement its X, but decrement follower 3's Y. On curve completion, exactly two party members skip follower 3's hop and select FinishObjectPath; other counts retain the helper's next stage. (C1, E-0358)
12:426F: Entry hop for follower 1: face it left, curve its Y and decrement its X, but decrement followers 2 and 3's Y. When the curve resets the phase, exactly one party member selects FinishObjectPath; otherwise continue with follower 2. (C1, E-0358)
12:4299: Entry hop for the player: face left, curve hPlayerY and decrement hPlayerX, but decrement all three followers' Y bytes. The curve helper advances after sixteen calls from phase 0; it does not move the followers' X bytes. (C1, E-0358)
12:42B5: DE points to an eight-bit coordinate. Store DE in wStepPtrLo/wStepPtrHi and far-call AddStepDeltaToPointedByte in bank $5F, which adds the curve entry for wScriptParam0 / 2 modulo 256. Advance the phase by two; only equality with $20 resets it and advances wScriptStep. Starting at phase 0 gives sixteen calls and zero net curve displacement; no bounds check protects other phases. (C1, E-0358)
12:42D7: Updates followers from the player's pre-move Y, then moves the player one pixel up. Advances only when the updated hPlayerY equals $50; the follower helper refreshes its targets at 16-pixel boundaries. (C1, E-0358)
12:42E9: After the fade, face the player and followers up and set follower Y to $C0, $D0, $E0. Set the player's moving bit and advance to the entry walk. The player's position is supplied by the preceding warp. (C1, E-0358)
12:4310: Decrements the player's and all three followers' Y bytes. When follower 3's updated Y equals $F0, request map $1A screen (2,0) at ($60,$B0), transition kind 0, and start the fade that advances the script. Otherwise return and keep walking. (C1, E-0358)
12:4346: Outgoing follower-3 hop: face it up and decrement the player's and all followers' Y bytes, then add the curve to follower 3's Y. Continue through AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase for stage timing. (C1, E-0358)
12:436E: Outgoing follower-2 hop: update the follower chain from the player's pre-move Y, decrement hPlayerY, and curve follower 2's Y. AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase handles completion; this stage does not explicitly change facing. (C1, E-0358)
12:438A: Outgoing follower-1 hop: update the follower chain from the player's pre-move Y, decrement hPlayerY, and curve follower 1's Y. Continue through AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase, without explicitly changing facing. (C1, E-0358)
12:43A6: Begin the outgoing path by setting the player's moving bit. Update followers from the player's pre-move Y, apply the curve to hPlayerY and decrement that Y. Falls through to AdvanceObjectPathHopPhase, which advances after sixteen calls from phase 0. (C1, E-0358)
12:43C6: Shared tail for the outgoing path hops: wScriptParam0 = (wScriptParam0 + 2) modulo 256. Only a result of $20 resets the phase and increments the eight-bit wScriptStep. From 0, completion takes sixteen calls; odd starting phases never satisfy the equality. The caller applies the curve before this tail. (C1, E-0358)
12:43DA: Runs SCRIPT_ARENA_ROUNDS through 26 stages: enter map $0B, walk the party into position, approach for three battles, stage the next opposing side between battles, then heal and leave. Shared ArenaScene stages also serve ArenaGridBattle. Message choices come from ArenaRankMessageTable; the next-round branches use the reused arena counter wRecordCapacity, not a farm-capacity query. (C1, E-0359)
12:4412: After the third battle, start column 7 of ArenaRankMessageTable, advance to its message wait, and decrement the eight-bit arena counter wRecordCapacity. Does not inspect a battle-result flag here. (C1, E-0359)
12:4420: Decrement the arena counter. If it becomes exactly 2, show closing column 7 and select stage 22; otherwise show column 5 and advance to stage 14. In both branches, increment wArenaRound, rebuild the remaining random foes and copy the current round into wEncounterMonsters, even when selecting the closing stage. (C1, E-0359)
12:444D: Decrement the arena counter. A result of exactly 2 selects closing column 7 and stage 22; every other result selects column 3 and the next stage. Both paths still increment wArenaRound and prepare the remaining round list and current foes. This condition alone does not establish a win or loss. (C1, E-0359)
12:447A: Hold field draw mask $0E while the opening message runs. Once idle, set the player moving and facing down at X = $40; put follower X at $40, first follower Y at 0 and followers 2/3 facing down. Increment wArenaFlags, reset the message byte for route timing, and advance to the shared entrance walk. The other coordinates and wScriptParam1 are left to the caller. (C1, E-0359)
12:44AF: Request map $0B screen (0,0), destination ($E0,0), transition kind 0, and start the fade that advances the script. Open message index wAreaGraphicsIndex + 5 in the current group, wrapping as a byte, then set wArenaFlags = $80 to select the special message row and sprite-selection path. (C1, E-0359)
12:44DB: Runs SCRIPT_ARENA_GRID_BATTLE through 27 stages, sharing the party entrance, battle approach, opposing-side arrival and exit with ArenaRounds. It adds an opening follow-up message. Between battles it refreshes the grid selection; rank 0 uses the fixed encounter list, other ranks use GridEncounterTable. wScriptStep selects the stage. (C1, E-0359)
12:4515: After leaving the arena, restart map music, queue talk-event group $65 index 1, and restore wScriptReturnBank/Lo/Hi into the active script request and pointer. Select command $F7, mark the script as in the data bank, and restore sprite-window clip mode 2. This stage serves both arena commands. (C1, E-0359)
12:4546: Heal the party through FullyHealParty, then request map $04 screen (1,0), destination ($40,$30), transition kind 3. Start the fade that advances to restoring the caller script. The heal helper uses the incoming SRAM bank and assumes a nonempty party. (C1, E-0359)
12:456A: Shared exit delay: increment wScriptParam0 once per call, queue sound $6D only when it becomes 1, and wait for exact equality with $3C. At $3C reset the counter and advance the stage. A fresh counter of 0 takes sixty calls; larger starting values wrap instead of being clamped. (C1, E-0359)
12:4587: After the third grid battle, show message-table column 7, advance to the shared message wait and decrement the reused arena counter wRecordCapacity. No battle-result flag is tested in this stage. (C1, E-0359)
12:4595: Show column 6 of ArenaRankMessageTable in the current group and advance to the shared message wait before the third battle approach. Used by both arena commands. (C1, E-0359)
12:459F: Show column 5, advance the stage and decrement the arena counter; SetupScreenCountPlusOneFromRecordCapacity immediately increments it again and updates the grid column from wAreaGraphicsIndex. Prepare the next three foes from the fixed list for rank 0, or GridEncounterTable for other ranks. (C1, E-0359)
12:45CC: Show column 4 of ArenaRankMessageTable, then advance to the shared message wait before the second battle approach. Does not change the current message group. (C1, E-0359)
12:45D6: Move arena object 0 upward one pixel, facing up, until its updated Y equals $30. Then face all four arena objects left, set field event kind 7, clear their moving bits, queue sound 0 and advance to the next battle announcement. Other Y values return without advancing. (C1, E-0359)
12:461A: Bring four arena objects into position, including slots not yet drawable. A timer borrowed from wMessageIndex reveals slot counts 2,3,4 at $10,$20,$30 and holds at $60. Each slot increments Y through byte wrap to $20, then X to $60, Y to $40 and X toward $70. Each slot whose updated X equals $70 increments wScriptStep separately; simultaneous arrivals can advance it multiple times in one call. (C1, E-0359)
12:469E: Set up the next map-$0B objects and their graphics from wEncounterMonsters. Request object palettes, show one slot initially, mark all four arena objects moving, disable the field-event updater, queue sound $6D, reset the borrowed message timer and advance to their entrance animation. (C1, E-0359)
